hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: Trump and Iran formally signed the ceasefire on June 15 with Strait reopening committed upon signing, oil plunged to multi-month lows, and the disruption premium has been structurally removed pending mine clearance logistics.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS-confirmed May CPI at 4.2 percent YoY — highest since April 2023 — with the Fed funds rate pinned at 3.50 to 3.75 percent and Warsh facing an FOMC decision on June 17 with zero room to cut amid accelerating inflation.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Dell Oro raised the global data center capex outlook above 1 trillion dollars for 2026 with Top 4 US hyperscalers up 78 percent YoY, but investor skepticism persists as capex now exceeds internal cash generation at 45 to 57 percent of revenue intensity and big tech has issued over 100 billion dollars in bonds to fund buildout.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold entered a volatile correction phase after peaking above 5500 per ounce in January and correcting nearly 15 percent in March to hold near 4400 per ounce, with the Iran peace deal removing a key geopolitical bid and oil-linked inflation premium fading, though central bank and ETF demand provide structural support.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: S and P Global confirms copper faces tightening concentrate markets and smelting bottlenecks with 2026 average price forecast above 12100 per metric ton on structural supply constraints despite a stronger dollar and high rates.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Uranium seller market is tightening with contract bands at 86 to 90 dollars per pound, Bank of America forecasts uranium prices rising 43 percent YoY to 105 dollars per pound in H2 2026 as utility buying returns, and IEA projects annual nuclear investment rising to 210 billion dollars by the mid-2030s.

ALAB.note: The AI connectivity thesis remains structurally intact — ALAB is joining the Nasdaq-100 on June 22 2026 which should attract passive inflows — but rising R and D operating expenses in the 112 to 118 million dollar range and a rich 20.26x forward price to sales ratio leave the stock vulnerable to any AI capex ROI disappointment.

POWL.note: The data center electrical infrastructure thesis is reinforced by the 1 trillion dollar capex outlook but the Hormuz deal has reduced the energy-sector power infrastructure premium, requiring validation that data center orders rather than oil and gas orders dominate the backlog.

MOD.note: Negative FCF of minus 101 million dollars remains a disqualifying quality flag and the Hormuz peace deal reduces the emergency energy infrastructure urgency that underpinned any speculative bull case.

GFS.note: The CHIPS Act foundry thesis continues to produce no new major contract catalysts and GFS remains a minor player at sub-scale versus TSM which controls over 50 percent of the global foundry market, making thesis drift from original buy rationale a live risk.

CRDO.note: CRDO delivered 272 percent YoY revenue growth in Q2 fiscal 2026 and guided Q3 revenues of 335 to 345 million dollars implying 27 percent sequential growth, with the company anticipating over 170 percent full-year growth and net income more than quadrupling — the thesis is executing cleanly and CRDO trades at a lower 14.98x forward P/S versus ALAB at 20.26x offering better relative value.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 134.48 with only $750M FCF remains priced for absolute perfection with no new licensing catalyst identified — the original licensing-expansion thesis has not produced incremental revenue inflections justifying this multiple.

S.note: SentinelOne at $268M FCF shows genuine cash generation improvement but the cybersecurity consolidation environment and competitive pressure from CrowdStrike and Microsoft continue to compress the path to premium pricing power.

ZS.note: Zscaler maintains the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1B but remains rated AVOID — the valuation at P/E 28.37 does not screen as expensive yet the growth deceleration thesis and intensifying platform competition have not resolved in ZS favor.

AXON.note: AXON at EV/EBITDA 379 with only $63M FCF has experienced complete thesis drift — the original law enforcement tech thesis has been overwhelmed by a valuation that requires hyper-growth compounding for a decade without any margin of safety — insider selling reported by TipRanks in early June 2026 is an additional red flag confirming the AVOID signal.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
